P001.text: Act on the next fortnight of deliveries, their handling histories and temperature measurements.

P002.text: Retain competing explanations: warming during staging or loading, warming in transit, warming while awaiting receipt, differences or errors in receiving measurement, and combinations of these.

P003.text: Acceptable loading-room records do not establish individual package temperatures at departure, and one receiving reading does not locate when warming occurred.

P004.text: Assume staff can identify a small sample of packages and record additional handling times; confirm logger suitability and permitted placement before using them.

P005.text: Before sampling, write down what evidence would support or weaken each explanation.

P006.text: Rotate the limited loggers through selected deliveries spanning all three bays, both carriers, shorter and longer routes, and different receiving methods; include deliveries without reported exceptions.

P007.text: Do not claim complete coverage or independently separable comparisons.

P008.text: Identify sampled packages and link each to its bay, carrier, route and receiving site.

P009.text: Check logger and receiving-device agreement under the same stable conditions, synchronize clocks, and choose a logging interval short enough to distinguish relevant handling stages within device capacity.

P010.text: Follow the same sampled package from refrigerated staging through loading, transit and receipt, recording staging exit, loading completion, departure, arrival and receiving-measurement times.

P011.text: Record logger placement, measurement method, relevant delays and accessible handling observations.

P012.text: Where feasible, pair the site's usual receiving reading with a promptly taken standardized reading on the same package using a suitable checked device and an approved method; record any difference in timing or measurement location.

P013.text: Review traces and paired readings as they become available, comparing similar deliveries and revising the competing explanations.

P014.text: During the investigation, reinforce required refrigeration, minimize avoidable unrefrigerated staging and receiving delays, and standardize approved receiving measurements.

P016.text: Follow existing food-handling and disposition requirements immediately for any suspected breach; do not wait for the investigation.

P017.text: Add more targeted temporary changes only when observations support the relevant stage, and track their effect without deliberately exposing food to unsafe conditions.

P018.text: Look for proposed discriminating patterns: a rise before departure supports staging/loading exposure; a rise after departure and before arrival supports transit exposure; a rise between arrival and the receiving reading supports receiving delay.

P019.text: These patterns require reliable stage times and a logger placement that meaningfully represents the sampled package's thermal conditions.

P020.text: Repeated disagreement between usual and standardized readings, especially when associated with method or device, supports measurement differences.

P021.text: Agreement between readings weakens that explanation for those observations.

P022.text: Multiple rises or a rise combined with measurement disagreement support multiple contributors.

P023.text: Bay room-temperature records, route duration alone, missing stage boundaries, or a logger measuring air while staff measure product may fail to distinguish explanations.

P024.text: Compare both exception and non-exception deliveries and actively seek observations inconsistent with the current leading explanation.

P025.text: Use the emerging patterns to prioritize the next investigation and proportionate handling changes, rather than declare a single cause.

P026.text: Repeated predeparture warming would justify concentrating observations on staging dwell and loading practices; transit warming would justify checking the implicated carrier's refrigeration operation and handling events; receiving-stage warming would justify prompt refrigerated receipt; reproducible measurement disagreement would justify device checks and method harmonization.

P027.text: Treat these as conditional follow-ups, not established findings.

P028.text: Lower an explanation's priority only when the observations could reasonably have detected its predicted pattern.

P029.text: At the fortnight's end, summarize supported, weakened and unresolved explanations, sampling gaps and interim actions.

P030.text: End the added two-week observation effort unless further work is authorized; if evidence remains inconclusive, propose a focused follow-up aimed at the unresolved distinction and retain required protective handling.

P031.text: This procedure can narrow plausible contributors but cannot guarantee a unique cause or demonstrate that every delivery meets requirements.

P032.text: A small, nonrandom sample may miss intermittent events and cannot establish their prevalence.

P033.text: Multiple readings from one package or trip are correlated, and bay, carrier, route and customer differences may be confounded.

P034.text: Logger placement, response lag, calibration uncertainty, clock error and single-package sampling limit detection and attribution; environmental temperature is not automatically product temperature.

P035.text: Paired methods may disagree because they measure different locations or at different times.

P036.text: Interim handling changes also alter the conditions being investigated, so improved outcomes alone do not prove causation.

P037.text: Retain alternatives absent a sensitive, relevant test, consider how frequently each condition occurs among sampled deliveries, and reopen the hypothesis set when observations fit none of the candidates.

P038.text: Stop or modify any added measurement procedure that compromises food handling or routine operations.
